raw.description: High fidelity scanner for php2shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619)
raw.readme_excerpt:
# php2shell-scanner

A command-line tool for detecting CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 in PHP applications.

## How It Works

The scanner sends a minimal multipart control request followed by up to three crafted multipart probes. The probes use PHP array keys nested 62 levels deep and increase from 1 MiB to 20 MiB, matching the detection logic used by Assetnote's internal scanner.

A target is reported vulnerable when the probe produces a PHP memory-exhaustion error, a differential empty HTTP 500, a PHP-FPM worker failure, or an advertised PHP version known to be unpatched. Initial 5xx responses, common request-rejection statuses, and nonempty HTTP 500 responses without the PHP fatal-error signature are not treated as crash signals.

The scanner tests `/index.php` by default. A path supplied in the URL is preserved, and `--path` or `--path-file` can test custom paths. phpMyAdmin targets are automatically retested at `/show_config_errors.php`. Redirects are not followed unless `--follow-redirects` is set.

### SAPI Modes

The default `--sapi auto` mode applies both mod_php and PHP-FPM verdict rules, matching the combined behavior of Assetnote's postmodules. Use `--sapi mod_php` or `--sapi fpm` to restrict detection to a known SAPI.

### Network Impact

Each tested path may receive a 42-byte control request and three probes totalling about 29 MiB. Probing stops as soon as the verdict is settled, and duplicate input URLs are scanned once.

## Requirements

- Python 3.9+
- h11
- tqdm

## Installation

```
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### Docker

Build the image:

```
docker build -t php2shell-scanner .
```

Run it with the same options as `scanner.py`:

```
docker run --rm php2shell-scanner -u https://example.com
```

Mount the current directory to read host lists and write results:

```
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/data" -w /data php2shell-scanner -l hosts.txt -o results.json
```

## Usage

Scan a single host:

```
python3 scanner.py -u https://example.com
```

Scan a list of hosts:

```
python3 scanner.py -l hosts.txt
```

Scan with multiple threads and save results:

```
python3 scanner.py -l hosts.txt -t 20 -o results.json
```

Scan with custom headers:

```
python3 scanner.py -u https://example.com -H "Authorization: Bearer token" -H "Cookie: session=abc"
```

Scan a custom path:

```
python3 scanner.py -u https://example.com --path /phpinfo.php
python3 scanner.py -u https://example.com --path /index.php --path /admin.php
python3 scanner.py -u https://example.com --path-file paths.txt
```

Use only PHP-FPM verdict rules:

```
python3 scanner.py -u https://example.com --sapi fpm
```

## Options

```
-u, --url         Single URL to check
-l, --list        File containing hosts (one per line)
-t, --threads     Number of concurrent threads (default: 10)
--timeout         Request timeout in seconds (default: 60)
-o, --output      Output file for results (JSON)
--all-results     Save all results, not just vulnerable hosts
-k, --insecure    Disable TLS certificate verification
--follow-redirects Follow HTTP redirects (up to 10 hops)
-H, --header      Custom header (can be used multiple times)
-v, --verbose     Show verdict reasons and response snippets
-q, --quiet       Only output vulnerable hosts
--no-color        Disable colored output
--sapi            Verdict rules: auto, mod_php, or fpm (default: auto)
--path            Custom path to test (can be used multiple times)
--path-file       File containing paths to test (one per line)
```

## Credits

The first, original discovery of php2shell is attributed to the Calif team. You can read their write up here: [https://calif.io/php2shell/](https://calif.io/php2shell/).

The scanner was built by the Assetnote Security Research Team using logic built for [Searchlight's Exposure Platform](https://www.slcyber.io/exposure).

## Output

Results are printed to the terminal. When using `-o`, vulnerable hosts are saved to a JSON file with the verdict reason and redacted HTTP request

raw.description: Turn any SVG into a professional 60 fps animation. A Claude Code skill that brings anything drawn to life: live faces, full-body acting and whole scenes, in React Native and SwiftUI.
raw.readme_excerpt: # Motion For Anything You Draw For designers and engineers who want to bring their apps and drawings to life. Making a drawing move is easy. Making it feel alive is hard: it has to breathe, look around, blink, shift its weight and act, without ever freezing or jumping. This skill helps your agent get there. It started as the method I used to bring the illustrations in my app to life, and grew into a way to animate anything drawn: characters and creatures, plants, cloth, fire, smoke, water, weather, lights, machines, icons, logos, charts and whole scenes. The animation above is drawn and animated entirely in code, with the templates in this repo. ## Install ```bash npx skills@latest add rossark0/rossark-motion-skill ``` ## Why use it? Agents don't animate like animators. Ask an agent to bring a character to life and it will often swap one drawing for another, so the face teleports from one expression to the next. It moves through each pose with its own eased tween, so the body stops dead at every pose. Everything moves in sync, like a machine. Blinks are so short they flicker, everything bounces, and a thin line shows across the face where two shapes meet. All these small things add up, and the result looks like a slideshow instead of something alive. This skill lists those mistakes and how to fix them: one clock for the whole scene, parts that turn around their real pivots, trailing parts that follow a beat later, idle life that never stops, smooth paths through key poses, small amplitudes and strong curves. When you have a reference video, it measures the motion frame by frame before building, because what makes a reference feel alive is often too small to see. For motion in an interface, it follows [Emil Kowalski's](https://github.com/emilkowalski/skills) rules and Benji Taylor's [Family values](https://benji.org/family-values). ## Reference - **[SKILL.md](./SKILL.md)**: The skill. Principles, recipes for every kind of subject, live faces, full-body acting, scenes that tell an action, motion in an interface, pitfalls, working from a reference video, and a workflow. - **[MOTION.md](./MOTION.md)**: A notes file for your project. Copy it next to your art and fill in Part 2 as you go: where the code is, your rules, what your art can't do, and how you check changes. The skill reads it first. - **[motion.ts](./templates/react-native/motion.ts)** and **[Motion.swift](./templates/swiftui/Motion.swift)**: The engine, for React Native and SwiftUI. Loop and one-shot clocks, `track`, `flow` (smooth acting through key poses), `seg`, `wave`, `loop`, `bell`, `seeded` and the curves. - **[liveFace.tsx](./templates/react-native/liveFace.tsx)** and **[LiveFace.swift](./templates/swiftui/LiveFace.swift)**: Live eyes and mouths that glide, blink and smile. You give them the geometry and the colours. - **[sheet.sh](./tools/sheet.sh)**: Contact sheets of a video at its full frame rate, to study timing or check your own render. - **[track_edges.py](./tools/track_edges.py)**: Measures a subject's edges frame by frame, to catch motion too small for the eye: a 2% jiggle, a float, a sway. - **[sample_colors.py](./tools/sample_colors.py)**: Reads exact colours from a video frame. - **[demo/](./demo)**: The scenes on this page, a phone frame and an offline renderer that turns them into MP4 and GIF. ## Demos **Reveal** ([source](demo/RevealScene.swift), [MP4](demo/reveal.mp4)), at the top of this page. Full-body acting in a phone frame, on one clock, in a 9-second loop at 60 fps: - a mystery silhouette floats in, its feet hanging limp, its shadow breathing with the height; - the kid hovers, falls with gravity, squashes on landing and keeps the volume; - poses flow into each other with `flow`, idle life n

raw.description: Extract huge archives in place: the archive shrinks as your files hatch, so you only need room for the output. ZIP, 7z, tar, split archives.
raw.readme_excerpt:
HatchZip

Extract huge archives in place. The archive shrinks as your files hatch,
so you only need free space for the output, not for the output and the archive.

Installation | Usage | Safety | How it works | Contributing

A 180 GB game download that unpacks to 200 GB needs 380 GB of disk with WinRAR, 7-Zip or `unzip`, because the archive and everything extracted from it have to exist at the same time. HatchZip needs a little over 200 GB. It extracts the archive from the end and cuts each finished part off the archive file as it goes, so the space the archive gives back is reused for the next files. It checks that the extraction will fit before it changes anything, keeps a safety margin of free space the whole way through, and can be stopped or crash at any moment and pick up where it left off. It reads ZIP, 7z, tar, `.tar.gz` and split archives. ### Get it No coding needed. **[Download for Windows](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x64-setup.exe)** (Windows 10 and 11), or for [macOS (Apple Silicon)](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-aarch64.dmg), [macOS (Intel)](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x86_64.dmg) and [Linux](#installation). 1. Run the installer. Windows may show "Windows protected your PC" because HatchZip is not code-signed yet: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. 2. Right-click the archive, choose **HatchZip**, then **Extract here**. On Windows 11 the menu is under **Show more options**. 3. Or open HatchZip from the Start menu, open the archive, and choose **Extract**. HatchZip shows whether the files will fit before it changes anything. The archive is used up as the files come out, so when it finishes, only the extracted files are left. ## Highlights The same 200 MB of game data (21 files), packed by the real tools, extracted on a 220 MiB disk with about 50 MB free: | Archive | `unzip` / 7-Zip | HatchZip | |---|---|---| | ZIP, 180 MB | `unzip` ran out of space at file 6 of 21 | Finished, every file byte-identical | | 7z from 7-Zip 25.01, `-ms=20m` (10 solid blocks) | Needs 380 MB | Finished in 0.64 s, every file byte-identical | | 7z split into 5 volumes of 40 MB | Needs 380 MB | Finished; volumes deleted one at a time, peak 210 MB used | | tar from GNU tar, 200 MB | Needs 400 MB | Finished in 0.12 s, every file byte-identical | | 7z from 7-Zip with default settings (1 solid block) | Needs 380 MB | Refused before touching anything: one solid block can't be freed until all of it is out, so it needs 200 MB free | | | Result | |---|---| | ZIP extraction speed, same data | 0.25 to 0.35 s, against 1.48 to 1.50 s for `unzip` 6.00, including an fsync `unzip` skips | | Crash safety | Killed at both unsafe moments of a batch at many points of each format's run; every resume finished with identical output | | Works on | Any filesystem that can shrink a file: ext4, btrfs, XFS, NTFS, APFS, and also exFAT and FAT32 USB drives | Measured on Fedora 43, Intel Core i7-14700HX, SK Hynix

raw.description: A tool to generate normal maps from any sprite and animated sprite sheet.
raw.readme_excerpt: # Sprite Fusion Sprite Normals - **Online version**: https://www.spritefusion.com/sprite-normals - **API**: https://www.spritefusion.com/docs/pixel-art-generator/api/generate-and-transform-images#normal-maps - **MCP**: https://www.spritefusion.com/docs/pixel-art-generator/api/mcp A tool to generate normal maps for pixel art sprites and animations. Written in Rust, available as a CLI and a WebAssembly library. ## Why ? **Normal maps let 2D sprites react to dynamic lighting. Ideal for 2.5D games.** Features: - ✅ Generate surface relief from a sprite's silhouette and shading. - ✅ Keep the original pixel resolution and transparency. - ✅ Process sprites, sprite sheets, and animations locally. ## Perfect for - **2D games** with moving lights and normal-mapped sprites. - **Pixel art animations** that need matching normal-map frames. - **Asset pipelines** using a native CLI or browser-based processing. ## 💻 CLI ### Build from source Requires [Rust](https://www.rust-lang.org/) 1.85 or newer. From this directory: ```bash cargo build --release --locked ``` The binary is available at `target/release/spritefusion-sprite-normals`. To install it locally: ```bash cargo install --path . --locked ``` ### Usage ```text spritefusion-sprite-normals ... [OPTIONS] ``` - ``: PNG sprites or sheets, GIF, or APNG files. - `-o `: Output normal PNG for one input. - `--output-dir `: Output directory for a batch. - `--normal-strength `: Overall strength. Defaults to `1.5`. - `--detail-strength `: Relief from painted shading. Defaults to `6`. - `--detail-scale `: Shading smoothing. Defaults to `0.6`. - `--shape-strength `: Silhouette volume. Defaults to `1.15`. - `--frame-size `: Isolate uniform PNG sheet cells. - `--normal-format directx`: Reverse the green channel. Defaults to OpenGL. - `--force`: Replace existing outputs. Input files are protected. ```bash spritefusion-sprite-normals sprite.png -o sprite_n.png spritefusion-sprite-normals sprites/*.png --output-dir normals spritefusion-sprite-normals sprite.png -o sprite_n.png --normal-strength 2 spritefusion-sprite-normals sheet.png --frame-size 32x32 -o sheet_n.png spritefusion-sprite-normals walk.gif -o walk_n.png ``` Without an output path, maps are saved beside their inputs as `_n.png`. Run `spritefusion-sprite-normals --help` for every option. ### Animations GIF and APNG inputs, and PNG sheets with `--frame-size`, produce three files: - `walk_n.png`: lossless normal-map atlas. - `walk_n.color.png`: color atlas with the same frame layout. - `walk_n.frames.json`: atlas dimensions, frame dimensions, columns, frame count, and timing. Frames are arranged in row-major order. `delays_ms` contains `[numerator, denominator]` pairs in milliseconds. PNG sheets keep their layout and receive a default 100 ms frame delay. Source loop counts are not exported. Normal PNGs are data textures: disable sRGB sampling in your engine. Use artwork at its native pixel resolution. raw.description: One 8 KB skill that replaces REA (Reverse Engineer Anything): plain CLI tools, no MCP. Benchmarked: 38% faster, 35% cheaper.
raw.readme_excerpt:
# leanrea

**One 8 KB skill file that does what [REA](https://github.com/morluto/rea) does: no MCP server, no 207 tools, no setup.**

REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) puts an MCP layer between your agent and tools it can already use: asar, otool, nm, `go version -m`, jadx, apktool, Ghidra, tshark, binwalk, sqlite3. leanrea drops that layer. It tells the agent which command is fastest for each kind of target, gives it ready-to-paste recon commands, and lists the traps that REA's code handles for you. The agent then runs the real tools itself.

|  | REA 6.5.0 | leanrea |
|---|---|---|
| What gets installed | 25 MB npm package + MCP server | one `SKILL.md` |
| Instructions | 23.5 KB skill + 48.8 KB references | 8 KB |
| Tools added to the agent | 207 (3.35 MB of definitions) | 0 (uses Bash) |
| Context for "Reply OK", all tools loaded | 400.7k tokens, $1.60 | 34.5k tokens, $0.09 |

## Benchmark

Claude Code headless (`claude -p`), Sonnet 5.5, macOS arm64. 4 reverse-engineering tasks × 3 reps × 3 arms, with the arms run side by side. Answers are graded against hand-made keys.

| arm | total wall time | cost | turns | tokens | score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **leanrea** | **388 s** | **$2.17** | **55** | **2.40 M** | 74/75 |
| no skill | 479 s | $2.21 | 81 | 3.11 M | 67/75 (one refusal) |
| REA (MCP + its skill) | 627 s | $3.36 | 124 | 5.93 M | 75/75 |

Against REA, leanrea had **38% less wall time, 35% lower cost, 56% fewer turns and 60% fewer tokens, at the same accuracy**. Its one partial miss named an older IPC channel instead of the v2 one (both channels exist).

The tasks:
- **electron**: trace a feature through a real Electron app's app.asar (native function → main-process class → IPC channels).
- **native**: inventory the exports, a TCC permission check and the single-instance lock of that app's native addon (`.node`).
- **go**: toolchain and dependency versions of a stripped `gh` binary.
- **deep**: from disassembly alone, the exact socket path format, wire protocol and peer authentication of that lock.

The same operation run through REA's CLI vs the raw command:

| operation | REA | raw |
|---|---|---|
| Go build info | 0.56 s | `go version -m`: 0.06 s |
| Mach-O overview | 3.32 s | otool + dyld_info + nm: 0.04 s |
| Electron app analysis (real desktop app) | fails on asar integrity until you pass a flag, then **47.9 s and 140 MB of JSON** | asar extract + `rg -uu`: 4.8 s, 24 KB |

Full tables, the context-overhead runs and caveats: [bench/BENCHMARK.md](bench/BENCHMARK.md). Raw per-run metrics: [bench/results/final.jsonl](bench/results/final.jsonl).

**Caveats:**
- Only 3 reps per cell, one model, one machine.
- REA was tested in its best case: Claude Code's deferred tool search loads MCP tools on demand. Agents that load every tool pay the 400k-token row.
- Ghidra, Hopper and jadx weren't installed, so the native tasks ran on Xcode tools for both arms.
- The plain model is already good at this. leanrea's gain over no skill (about 19% faster, 32% fewer turns) is smaller than its gain over REA.

## Install

```sh
npx skills add aicodeking/leanrea
```

This uses the [skills CLI](https://skills.sh). It finds the `leanrea` skill and asks which agents to install it for: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and the others it supports.

Common variants:
```sh
npx skills add aicodeking/leanrea -g                    # install for your user, in every project
npx skills add aicodeking/leanrea -a claude-code -y     # Claude Code only, no prompts
npx skills add aicodeking/leanrea -g -a '*' -y          # every supported agent, user level
npx skills update leanrea                               # pull the latest version later
```

Manual install, if you prefer:
```sh
git clone https://github.com/aicodeking/leanrea
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -R leanrea/leanrea ~/.claude/skills/
```
If an agent has no skills support, paste `leanrea/SKILL.md` into its rules or system prompt; it is plain text.

Use it:
```
/leanrea How d

raw.readme_excerpt:
# Tigris > **最新正式版 v2.0.6（2026-10-24）**：新增「最近打开的 App 自动置顶」开关，默认关闭，允许手动固定应用顺序；正式安装包与校验文件统一带版本号。详见 [2.0.6 更新说明](docs/releases/v2.0.6.md)。上版 [2.0.5 桌面守护优化](docs/releases/v2.0.5.md) 仍然保留，雷鸟 #14 仍待对应型号复测。

**语言：** [简体中文](README.md) · [English](README.en.md) 把 Android TV 的桌面换成 tvOS 26 的样子：沉底的 Liquid Glass Dock、Top Shelf 式顶部内容、毛玻璃控制中心、风景照片背景和相框屏保。 > 十二生肖开源系列第三个项目：虎。Tigris 是拉丁语和希腊语里的“老虎”。 - 官网：**[tigris-tv.pages.dev](https://tigris-tv.pages.dev)** - 最新正式版：**[v2.0.6 Release](https://github.com/lesnolie/Tigris/releases/tag/v2.0.6)**（[标准版 APK](https://github.com/lesnolie/Tigris/releases/download/v2.0.6/Tigris-v2.0.6.apk) · [TCL / 雷鸟守护版 APK](https://github.com/lesnolie/Tigris/releases/download/v2.0.6/Tigris-guard-v2.0.6.apk) · [SHA-256 校验文件](https://github.com/lesnolie/Tigris/releases/download/v2.0.6/SHA256SUMS-v2.0.6.txt)） [![观看 Tigris 宣传片](docs/screenshots/film.jpg)](https://tigris-tv.pages.dev/#film) ▶ [观看 42 秒宣传片](https://tigris-tv.pages.dev/#film)（在官网播放，有声音） --- ## 1. 展示与功能 ![主屏幕](docs/screenshots/home.jpg) | 顶部内容（Top Shelf） | 展开全部 App | |---|---| | ![顶部内容](docs/screenshots/shelf.jpg) | ![展开全部 App](docs/screenshots/grid.jpg) | | **控制中心** | **相框 / 屏保** | | ![控制中心](docs/screenshots/cc.jpg) | ![相框屏保](docs/screenshots/frame.jpg) | ### v2.0.6 更新内容 - **应用顺序可以固定**：主屏幕设置 → App →「最近打开的 App 自动置顶」。默认关闭，不再因为启动应用而改变顺序；需要自动置顶时可自行开启。切换选项不会重置现有布局和文件夹。 - **正式安装包带版本号**：标准版 `Tigris-v2.0.6.apk`、守护版 `Tigris-guard-v2.0.6.apk`；同版本的校验文件为 `SHA256SUMS-v2.0.6.txt`。应用内更新与安装脚本兼容新版和旧版命名。 - **稳定升级**：沿用现有正式版签名，兼容签名一致的覆盖安装；不需要卸载清数据。完整变化见 [v2.0.6 更新说明](docs/releases/v2.0.6.md)。 ### 2.0.4 新增 - **应用文件夹**：长按应用创建文件夹，支持移入、移出、改名和解散。 - **上传头像**：主屏幕设置 → 上传头像，用手机扫码上传或恢复默认头像。 - **统一更新中心**：在同一个页面检查 Tigris 和 MiracastReceiver 的 GitHub 正式版，可手动下载，也可尝试自动安装。 - **下滑磨砂效果**：应用列表下滑时背景逐渐虚化，Dock 保留玻璃底板并随第一排自然滑出屏幕；右上角时间和控件同步离屏，不吸顶、不占用焦点。 - **内置默认素材**：内置默认开机视频和设置页背景；设置背景的主体向左偏移，为右侧按钮留出空间。自定义素材优先，已有配置保留。 ### 核心功能 - **主屏幕**：5 列 16:9 圆角图标，选中时弹性放大、倾斜并带高光和投影。右上角显示时间、网络与可选头像；时间支持 12 / 24 小时制，也可改成左上角大时钟或隐藏。 - **Liquid Glass Dock**：第一排应用放在液态玻璃 Dock 中，下一排露出上沿。玻璃模糊、边缘折射和高光会按当前背景预先生成，低配电视可改用更省性能的样式。 - **顶部内容**：选中 Dock 中的云视听小电视或斗鱼时，上半屏轮播对应的热门内容。数据来自服务公开的网页接口，使用前需要安装对应的 TV 版 App。 - **主屏幕设置**：仿 tvOS 的分组布局，可分别调整时钟、聚焦动画、控制中心样式、背景、相框、开机动画、头像和桌面守护。 - **最近打开自动置顶（可开启）**：v2.0.6 首次安装或从旧版升级时默认关闭；可在「主屏幕设置 → App → 最近打开的 App 自动置顶」开启，之后成功打开的 App 或文件夹会移到第一位。关闭后固定当前排序，长按「编辑主屏幕」可自行调整；已有的个人布局和开关选择会保留。 - **编辑、文件夹与删除**：长按图标可移动、放入文件夹或删除。电视预装 App 也可用 `pm uninstall --user 0` 从当前用户空间移除，并可在设置中恢复；系统运行必需组件受到保护。 - **控制中心**：遥控器返回键或右上角按钮打开，提供网络、待机、关机、重启、释放内存、相框、设置、亮度、音量和 HDMI 输入源。低配机型可切换成深色面板。 - **背景与手机上传**：支持必应每日风景、360 壁纸、Wallhaven 全年龄二次元、公有领域名画、纯色渐变、手机相册照片和自定义图片链接。手机扫码页面还支持上传头像、开机视频和设置页背景。 - **相框与航拍屏保**：照片全屏轮播，画面缓慢平移缩放，时间文字定时移动以减少 OLED 烙印；也可在线播放 Apple TV 航拍视频，支持左右键切换，断网时回到照片。 - **HDMI 输入源上屏**：在控制中心把常用 HDMI 口固定到主屏幕，按一下即可切换。 - **软件更新与投屏**：每 6 小时检查 Tigris 和 [MiracastReceiver](https://github.com/weekdayjast/MiracastReceiver) 的正式版。更新前验证包名、系统版本、递增版本号和签名；不会自动卸载、不清数据、不接受降级。电视系统仍可能要求一次安装来源授权或每次确认。 - **内存清理**：支持定时清理和待机清理，保留名单可在设置中修改。 ### 素材与商标说明 仓库为界面展示打包了默认开机视频，并在线播放 Apple TV 航拍内容。这些素材不附带 Apple 或任何第三方的额外授权，也不代表 Tigris 与 Apple 有关联。对外分发、商用或再发布时，请确认素材授权；也可以在设置中改用 Tigris 字样动画或上传自己拥有权利的视频。截图中的影视封面、摄影作品和第三方图标版权归各自权利人所有。 ## 2. 安装指南 > [!CAUTION] > **不要停用或卸载电视原厂桌面。** 尤其是小米 / Redmi 的 `com.mitv.tvhome`（PatchWall）；强行停用后，部分电视会开机黑屏，只能通过 ADB 恢复。正确做法是保留原桌面，使用 Tigris 的默认 HOME 或桌面守护。 > > **手动修改前先记录原配置。** 至少保存默认 HOME、屏保、无障碍服务和通知监听的原值。`install.sh` 会自动保存快照；手动安装请自行记录，缺少记录时不要猜包名。 > > **只在自己的局域网开启 ADB。** 不要把电视调试端口暴露到公网。 > > **签名不一致时不要直接卸载。** `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE` 表示新 APK 与原包签名不同；直接卸载会丢失设置和授权。应先找到原签名密钥重新签名。 Tigris 官方包要求 **Android 9 / API 28 或更高**，不支持 LG webOS、三星 Tizen、华为鸿蒙智慧屏等非 Android 系统。 ### 2.1 打开电视的 ADB 调试 1. 让电脑和电视连接同一个局域网。 2. 在电视的网络或关于页面找到 IP 地址，例如 `192.168.1.20`。 3. 按品牌打开 ADB。 | 电视 | 开启方法 | |---|---| | **索尼 BRAVIA** | 设置 → 系统 → 关于 → 在 Android TV 操作系统版本上连按确认键 7 次；再到 设置

# The Day Trader skill

11 Claude skills for day trading: scan thousands of charts, track breaking news, time every entry and exit, and replay every outcome before you risk a dollar.

Free, MIT, no signup, no API key. The tools are plain Python that read free
public data: Yahoo Finance charts, Nasdaq Trader's symbol lists, SEC EDGAR
and the House Clerk.

One scans thousands of charts for setups. Another tracks breaking news on
every stock you watch. One watches a setup bar by bar and tells you the moment
to get in, and another sets your stop and your target before you do. And the
craziest one is the Time Machine: before you risk a dollar, it replays the
rest of the session 10,000 times from the stock's own recent bars, plus every
past day the same setup fired, and tells you the honest odds.

And no trade goes through until you say yes. Nothing in this pack can place
an order on its own. Paper trading is the default.

> **Looking for the original Trader skill?** Copy an investor's 13F, the
> stock screener, tax lots and rebalancing live in
> [github.com/Jakeschincariol/trader-skill](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/trader-skill).
> This repo is its day-trading sequel: the Trader skill v2.

## Install

Paste this into Claude:

```
https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/day-trader-skill

install skill
```

Or as a plugin, in Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add Jakeschincariol/day-trader-skill
/plugin install day-trader-skill@day-trader-skill
```

Claude Code namespaces plugin skills, so installed as a plugin they show up as
`/day-trader-skill:trader-scanner` and so on. Copy the folders instead if you want
plain `/trader-scanner`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/day-trader-skill.git
cp -r day-trader-skill/trader-* ~/.claude/skills/
```

Project-local instead of global: copy the same folders into your repo's
`.claude/skills/`. No Claude Code at all? Paste any single `SKILL.md` at the
top of a chat and it runs as a mode. You lose the Python tools, but the method
works.

The tools need Python 3.8 or newer. Nothing to pip install. The SEC tools
(news filings, the analyst) ask you to identify yourself: put your name and
email in `trader/config.json` (`"sec_user_agent": "Your Name you@example.com"`)
or in the `SEC_USER_AGENT` environment variable.

## The eleven

| command | job | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/trader-scanner` | Chart Scanner | Scans thousands of charts for setups: opening-range breakouts, flags, oversold bounces. |
| `/trader-news` | News Monitor | Tracks breaking news on every stock you watch and flags what moves it. |
| `/trader-entry` | Entry Timer | Watches a setup bar by bar and tells you the moment to get in. |
| `/trader-exit` | Exit Planner | Sets your stop and your target before you enter, so you know when to get out. |
| `/trader-timemachine` | Time Machine | Replays every possible outcome of a trade before you risk a dollar: 10,000 simulated sessions plus every past time the setup fired. |
| `/trader-risk` | Risk Manager | Checks every trade against your limits and stops anything over them. |
| `/trader-budget` | Budget Manager | Sizes every position to your budget and your max loss per trade. |
| `/trader-broker` | Order Executor | Sends approved orders to your broker, paper trading by default, never without your yes. |
| `/trader-alerts` | Price Alerts | Rings when a price, a stop or the opening bell hits. |
| `/trader-analyst` | Earnings Analyst | Reads earnings reports and sums up what changed. |
| `/trader-pelosi` | Pelosi Tracker | Reads Congress's stock-trade disclosures the minute they are filed. |

## How to use it

Everything lands in a `trader/` folder in your project, and each skill reads

raw.description: Run many Claude Code and Codex agents side by side, in one sidebar that tells you which one needs you. An unofficial fork of Warp.
raw.readme_excerpt:
Run many Claude Code and Codex agents side by side, in one calm sidebar that tells you which one needs you.

Harp is an unofficial fork of the open-source [Warp](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp) terminal. It replaces the tab bar with a sidebar built for long-running coding agents and keeps the rest of Warp as it is. ## What it adds

Agent states at a glance

Each row shows whether its Claude Code or Codex session is working, waiting for you or done, with an unread mark until you look. A dot means background work is still running; a moon marks a tab you set aside. Cmd+R renames a tab.

Groups that stay put

Put tabs into named groups. With the tmux integration on, the group and the order are stored on the tmux sessions, so they survive a restart and other tmux clients see the same layout.

Limit rings

Two rings per provider in the footer: the 5 hour window and the weekly limit. Hover one for the numbers and reset times. Codex's come from its own session logs, Claude's from Claude Code's status line (see below). Harp fetches nothing and reads no credentials.

Phone-friendly tmux

Tabs attached to tmux follow their session: name, group, read and inactive flags. A session started elsewhere, for example from your phone over ssh, can ask for a tab with tmux set-option @warp_adopt 1.
Everything else is upstream Warp, including its AI and cloud features (agents, Warp Drive, session sharing, login). They talk to Warp's servers exactly as upstream does; Harp adds no servers of its own. Logging in through Harp is untested. ## Install **Download:** grab the latest `Harp-.dmg` from [Releases](../../releases/latest) and drag Harp into Applications. Harp has its own bundle id (`com.dominikmartn.Harp`), URL scheme (`harp://`) and settings folder (`~/.harp`), so it runs next to Warp without sharing anything. **Updates:** Harp checks the latest GitHub release every 10 minutes, the same way Warp checks its own server. When the release's version is newer than `version` in `app/Cargo.toml` of the running build, Harp downloads its DMG in the background, checks that it is signed by Harp's Developer ID team, and offers to restart into it. raw.description: Agent skill for native Nintendo Switch game porting to Apple Silicon macOS, iPadOS and iOS with Rust and Metal
raw.readme_excerpt:
# NS 游戏 Apple ARM 原生移植 Skill

面向 AI 编程助手的指令型 skill，用于将 Nintendo Switch 游戏适配到 Apple Silicon macOS、iPadOS 和 iOS。以 Rust 原生兼容层与 Metal 为核心，覆盖版本识别、AArch64 离线改写、Horizon 服务、NVN → Metal、输入音频、部署及实机验收。

## 安装与使用

将仓库克隆到助手的 skills 目录。例如安装到 Codex：

```bash
git clone https://github.com/realskyrin/ns-game-apple-arm-port.git ~/.codex/skills/ns-game-apple-arm-port
```

重新加载助手后，在目标游戏移植项目中使用：

```text
使用 $ns-game-apple-arm-port 检查当前游戏版本和移植基础，按 Rust 与 Metal 架构先集中完成当前目标内的全量代码修改，再统一测试、集中修复与定向复测，并记录实际运行证据与未验证项。
```

也可以直接让助手读取 [SKILL.md](SKILL.md)。目标仓库、资源位置与设备由具体任务提供。

## 默认工作节奏

1. 盘点当前目标的已知缺口和依赖，连续完成跨模块实现、调用方与平台配置。
2. 修改完成后统一检查、构建、测试和游戏验收，汇总失败；实现期间不逐文件或逐补丁启动测试。
3. 按根因集中修复，定向复测失败项和受影响项，再用最终构建确认受影响的游戏路径。

只有缺失关键事实、后续实现无法可靠继续时，才提前执行最小探针。全量修改以当前任务为边界，最终仍需真实运行证据，不将代码完成或构建成功等同于可玩。

## 内容

- [SKILL.md](SKILL.md)：工作流程、语言架构、诊断与交付要求。
- [架构与推进](references/architecture-and-workflow.md)：Rust 模块边界、版本适配与最短验证路径。
- [执行层与平台](references/runtime-and-platforms.md)：装载、ABI、服务、线程、平台部署与音频。
- [图形与排障](references/graphics-and-debugging.md)：NVN → Metal、纹理一致性、shader 与性能诊断。
- [验收与案例](references/validation-and-cases.md)：证据阶梯、记录模板与可迁移经验。
- [Codex 元数据](agents/openai.yaml)：名称、简介与默认提示词。

本仓库提供移植方法与诊断指导，不包含游戏、密钥、固件、兼容层实现或构建产物。游戏资源保持本地；仅交付有权分发的内容。构建、启动、画面、输入、音频与可玩性分别以实际证据验收。

## 致谢与参考

本 Skill 将本地游戏移植实践整理为通用工作方法。感谢以下项目公开原生执行、兼容层和平台适配的设计与实现；其中经验来源与相关工程参考分别说明如下：

- **[c22dev/mush8](https://github.com/c22dev/mush8)**：本 Skill 的 Rust/Cargo 模块划分提炼自基于 mush8 的本地 BOTW 移植实践。mush8 的 ARM64 离线改写、Horizon 宿主、NVN → Metal，以及 macOS 运行时装载与 iOS 构建期链接的分工，是相关架构经验的来源。
- **[jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile)**：本 Skill 所总结的早期 iPad 移植实践曾参考其原游戏 ARM64 代码改写、宿主服务、离线 shader 转换与 iOS 壳层路线；跨游戏复用的是方法与边界，游戏专用地址、补丁和逻辑仍需独立核实。
- **[ly05010419/MacNativeGames](https://github.com/ly05010419/MacNativeGames)**：作为相关工程参考，展示了用户自备资源、按版本核验模块、原生执行与 Metal 图形适配、独立缓存/存档，以及区分构建检查和真实游戏验收的实践。它与本 Skill 的路线相呼应；当前未确认它是本 Skill 原始编写时的直接来源。

以上致谢说明思路与实践的关联，不表示这些项目为本 Skill 背书，也不表示本仓库包含其运行时代码。

## 许可证

本仓库的原创 Skill 指令、文档与元数据采用 [MIT License](LICENSE)。

参考项目及其代码仍遵循各自许可证：mush8 为 GPL v3，d2r-mobile 与 MacNativeGames 为 MIT；其中第三方组件以各项目的许可声明为准。本仓库的 MIT 许可不覆盖这些外部代码或任何游戏程序、资源、密钥及固件。
